title: Ethiopian Popcorn
community: All of Ethiopia — the cinema and coffee ceremony popcorn
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Popcorn — popping corn dry-popped or with minimal oil in a covered pan, seasoned with salt or a pinch of berbere. An integral part of the Ethiopian coffee ceremony — popcorn is always served alongside coffee, a tradition unique to Ethiopia.
longDesc: Ethiopian coffee ceremony popcorn is one of the most charming food traditions in the world — at every Ethiopian coffee ceremony, alongside the incense and the coffee, popcorn is popped and served. It is the universal snack of Ethiopian social life.
steps: Heat a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Add oil if using — or pop dry.
Add 3 kernels. When they pop, add remaining corn.
Pop 3—4 minutes until popping slows to 2—3 seconds between pops.
Season immediately with salt (and berbere if using).
chefTips: Shake the pan continuously — prevents burning.
Remove from heat when popping slows — lingering causes burnt corn.
Berbere popcorn is a modern Ethiopian café favourite.
commonMistakes: Not shaking — burns on the bottom.
cookingScience: Popcorn kernels contain a water droplet within a hard starch endosperm. At 180°C, the water vaporises rapidly, building pressure until the hull ruptures and the starch gelatinises and expands up to 40x the original volume.
sustainabilityTips: Popping corn — minimal processing, no packaging.
culturalNote: Ethiopian popcorn at the coffee ceremony is one of the most distinctive food traditions in the world — the unique combination of incense smoke, coffee being roasted and brewed, and popcorn being popped all simultaneously is the multi-sensory experience of Ethiopian hospitality. No other culture serves popcorn at its most important social ritual.
